title: Fabric Spark session architecture
purpose: How notebooks and job definitions acquire managed Spark compute through starter or custom pools, run driver and executor work against OneLake, and expose lifecycle and monitoring signals.
accessibleSummary: Fabric Spark session architecture. Notebook or job definition; Capacity vCore envelope; Starter or custom pool; Driver and executors; Native and JVM execution; OneLake Delta I/O; Session lifecycle risk.
longDescription: How notebooks and job definitions acquire managed Spark compute through starter or custom pools, run driver and executor work against OneLake, and expose lifecycle and monitoring signals.

nodes.label: Notebook or job definition
nodes.summary: Interactive notebooks and scheduled job definitions submit Spark applications.
nodes.detail: The authoring item carries code, environment, and execution configuration into a session request.
nodes.whyItMatters: The entry point determines scheduling and reproducibility needs.

evidence.note: Spark Job Definitions provide a configured, schedulable way to run Spark workloads.
Fabric Spark supports notebook and job sessions.

drill.example: A nightly job definition submits a bronze-to-silver transform.
failureModes: Notebook-only state makes production execution irreproducible.

nodes.label: Capacity vCore envelope
nodes.summary: The assigned Fabric capacity bounds Spark compute available to its workspaces.
nodes.detail: Pool configuration and concurrent sessions consume from that shared envelope.
nodes.whyItMatters: Capacity is an outer constraint on pool scale, not a per-job performance guarantee.

evidence.note: Fabric capacity units determine the Spark vCore envelope available to configured pools.

drill.example: Two workspace jobs contend for the same capacity's Spark envelope.
failureModes: Aggregate pool maxima exceed practical concurrent capacity.

nodes.label: Starter or custom pool
nodes.summary: Starter pools favor preconfigured fast acquisition; custom pools expose node and scale controls.
nodes.detail: Fabric chooses prewarmed or on-demand acquisition according to the selected configuration and availability.
nodes.whyItMatters: Pool choice balances startup consistency with workload-specific tuning.

evidence.note: Fabric provides preconfigured starter pools and configurable custom Spark pools.

drill.example: Exploration uses a starter pool while a scheduled workload uses a tuned custom pool.
failureModes: A starter pool falls back to on-demand acquisition under demand.

nodes.label: Driver and executors
nodes.summary: A pool has a head node hosting the driver and worker nodes hosting executors.
nodes.detail: The driver plans and coordinates work; executors run tasks over partitions.
nodes.whyItMatters: Understanding roles directs memory and failure diagnosis.

evidence.note: Fabric Spark pools use a head node for the driver and worker nodes for executors.

drill.example: The driver builds stages and four executors process table partitions.

nodes.label: Native and JVM execution
nodes.summary: Supported SQL operators can run through the native engine while unsupported segments fall back to JVM Spark.
nodes.detail: Gluten translates supported physical-plan segments to Substrait for Velox; correctness continues through fallback.
nodes.whyItMatters: Mixed execution explains why acceleration varies within one job.

evidence.note: Gluten converts supported Spark plan segments for Velox; unsupported segments fall back to JVM execution.

processing: Route supported operators to native execution
drill.example: A scan and aggregation run natively while one unsupported expression falls back.
failureModes: Precision-sensitive behavior differs across native and JVM paths.

nodes.label: OneLake Delta I/O
nodes.summary: Spark reads and writes lakehouse Delta tables in OneLake.
nodes.detail: Delta commits connect parallel task output to a versioned table state consumed by other Fabric engines.
nodes.whyItMatters: Shared storage is the durable hand-off; cluster disks are temporary execution state.

evidence.note: Fabric Spark writes Delta tables and supports Fabric-specific layout optimization.
Spark DataFrame write APIs commit managed Delta table changes.

drill.example: The job appends validated orders to a silver Delta table.
failureModes: Partial output or conflicting write fails the commit.

nodes.label: Session lifecycle risk
nodes.summary: Idle expiry and deallocation end the session; startup and library personalization affect schedules.
nodes.detail: Operational design must include acquisition time, session timeout, run telemetry, and retry behavior.
nodes.whyItMatters: Ignoring lifecycle turns a correct job into an unreliable service.

evidence.note: Sessions have configurable expiry and pools deallocate after inactivity; acquisition time varies by pool configuration.

drill.example: An orchestration timeout is set above expected custom-pool acquisition and library setup.
failureModes: A scheduler treats cluster startup as job failure and duplicates the run.
